quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: No two families in a row now, so decide first: vowel or consonant? Then listen.
quests.explanation: You heard "deep": a long, tense vowel with the mouth in a slight smile. "Dip" stops sooner and stays relaxed.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Two things separate these vowels: duration and tongue tension. /iː/ is held longer and sounds bright and tight; /ɪ/ is clipped and sounds softer, almost muffled by comparison.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the jaw nearly closed for both, but make /iː/ tighter: lips spread, tongue pushed high and forward. /ɪ/ needs no effort at all - let everything go slack.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Ignore the rest of the phrase and listen for the opening consonant.
quests.explanation: "Ramp" started with the tongue tip pulled back and untouching. "Lamp" would tap the ridge behind the upper teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /l/ sounds clear and light; /r/ sounds darker and slightly rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the tongue tip: contact for /l/, hover for /r/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The change is in the middle, between the two vowels. Hiss or buzz?
quests.explanation: In this phrase you heard "leaving", with a soft buzz between the vowels. "Leafing" has a breathy /f/ instead.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The vowel before /v/ is slightly longer than before /f/.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the friction gentle for /v/ and stronger for /f/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same first and last sound. Listen only to the vowel: long and open, or short?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "calm": a long, wide-open vowel. "Come" is quick and flat.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for a short, blunt vowel (/ʌ/) versus a longer, open one (/ɑː/) that seems to come from further back in the throat.
quests.mouthPosition: The lips stay neutral for both vowels; the real change is the jaw, which drops much further for /ɑː/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the vowel's length and the softness of the ending.
quests.explanation: "Lab" holds the vowel slightly longer and closes the lips softly. "Lap" clips the vowel and shuts crisply.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Don't wait for a burst at the end: listen to how long the vowel lasts before the lips close.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the throat relaxed for /b/ and tighten the closure for /p/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The beginning is either bare or has a hiss in front of it.
quests.explanation: That was "lip": the tongue tip touched the ridge right at the start, with no hiss. "Slip" would put an /s/ in front.
quests.vowelTensionRule: After /s/, /p t k/ lose their puff of air, so the cluster sounds different from the plain word.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue tip near the ridge for both /s/ and the following /t/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both fit the phrase. Does the vowel glide or stay steady?
quests.explanation: "Taste" glides upward as the jaw closes toward the /s/. "Test" is short and stays put.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A pure vowel (/e/) keeps one position; a diphthong (/eɪ/) slides and ends with a small 'ee' closing.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the jaw close during /eɪ/; during /e/ it stays put.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Notice the vowel length and whether your lips would need to round.
quests.explanation: The word was "stalk": a long vowel with the lips clearly rounded. "Stock" is short and more open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Compare length first: /ɔː/ is held, /ɒ/ is clipped. Then compare colour: /ɔː/ sounds closed and rounded, /ɒ/ sounds open and plain.
quests.mouthPosition: Imagine the shape of an oval mouth for /ɒ/ and a small circle for /ɔː/, then hold the second one longer.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for something after the /d/.
quests.explanation: "Hands" ends with a buzzing /z/ after the /d/. "Hand" stops on the /d/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The final /s/ or /z/ adds a whole extra sound to the end of the word, creating a consonant cluster. Listen for a hissing or buzzing tail after the word.
quests.mouthPosition: End the base word cleanly, then add a quick /s/ or /z/ with the tongue tip near the ridge. Voice the ending after voiced sounds and whisper it after voiceless ones.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both vowels are long. Is the mouth half open or wide open?
quests.explanation: Here, "barn" opened wide, low and back. "Burn" would be half open and central.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The difference is jaw opening and tongue position: /ɜː/ is half open and central, /ɑː/ is fully open and further back.
quests.mouthPosition: Open the mouth wider and lower the tongue to go from /ɜː/ to /ɑː/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the vowel begin rounded, or open and neutral?
quests.explanation: It was "voice": the lips began rounded before spreading. "Vice" starts with the jaw wide open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The start of /ɔɪ/ sounds dark and round; the start of /aɪ/ sounds open and bright.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the lips go from round to spread during /ɔɪ/; in /aɪ/ they never round.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Lips or tongue? Listen to the first sound.
quests.explanation: "Wheel" starts with the lips rounded and opening. "Reel" starts with a curled tongue and hardly any lip movement.
quests.vowelTensionRule: For /w/ the lips do the work; for /r/ the tongue does.
quests.mouthPosition: Watch your lips: they move a lot for /w/ and much less for /r/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The words share a start but not their rhythm. Where does the beat fall?
quests.explanation: "Dessert" puts its beat on the second syllable, with a long /ɜː/. "Desert" stresses the first syllable and ends weakly.
quests.vowelTensionRule: English stress changes vowel quality and length: the stressed syllable is louder, longer and clearer, while unstressed syllables reduce toward /ə/ or /ɪ/. The words differ in where the strong syllable falls.
quests.mouthPosition: Make the stressed syllable longer, louder and slightly higher in pitch, and let the other syllable shrink.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Short and loose, or long and tight?
quests.explanation: You heard "suit": long, with tightly rounded lips. "Soot" is short with loose lips.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʊ/ is short with loosely rounded lips and a tongue that is not quite high; /uː/ is long, with the lips pushed forward into a tight circle and the tongue high at the back.
quests.mouthPosition: For /uː/ push the lips forward into a small, tight round and lift the back of the tongue high. For /ʊ/ keep the lips only loosely rounded and cut the sound short.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for a buzz at the start.
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "junk" started with a buzzing /dʒ/ that you could feel in your throat. "Chunk" starts breathier.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /tʃ/ is crisper, /dʒ/ is heavier.
quests.mouthPosition: Round the lips slightly for both.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Round and open, or thin and tight?
quests.explanation: That was "hop", with rounded lips and a dropped jaw. "Hip" is tight and bright.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɪ/ is a high front vowel with spread or neutral lips; /ɒ/ is an open back vowel with slightly rounded lips. They differ in almost every way: height, backness and lip shape.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɪ/ keep the jaw nearly shut and the tongue forward. For /ɒ/ drop the jaw and pull the tongue back with a little lip rounding.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for a short sound after the /n/.
quests.explanation: "Cleaned" finishes with a quick /d/ after the /n/. "Clean" ends on the hum.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A short /t/ or /d/ closes the past-tense word, and it may be unreleased before a consonant.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the ending short and soft.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: There's a spill on the floor.
quests.hint: Is there a hiss before the lip pop?
quests.explanation: The word was "spill": a hiss, and then a soft /p/ with no puff. "Pill" begins straight with a breathy /p/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Adding or dropping /s/ at the start of a cluster changes the word: /sp/, /st/, /sk/ begin with a hiss that is followed by an unaspirated stop. Without /s/, the stop is aspirated and comes first.
quests.mouthPosition: Start with a clear hiss with the tongue behind the teeth, then move directly into the stop. Without /s/, begin with the stop and release with a puff.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll meet you at the bank.
quests.hint: Compare the vowels: dull and short or bright and wide?
quests.explanation: This time, the word was "bank", with a wide, bright vowel. "Bunk" is short and dull.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /æ/ is a front, open vowel made with the jaw low and lips slightly spread; /ʌ/ is a central, relaxed vowel that needs far less mouth opening.
quests.mouthPosition: For /æ/ drop the jaw and pull the corners of the mouth a little sideways. For /ʌ/ keep the mouth relaxed and only slightly open, with the tongue resting in the middle.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the air stop at the start, or keep flowing?
quests.explanation: It was "tree": the tongue tip stopped the air with a burst, then curled for /r/. "Three" starts with soft friction at the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /t/ is abrupt; /θ/ is gradual and airy.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the air flow continuously for /θ/ and burst for /t/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both end in a hum. Do the lips close?
quests.explanation: The word was "lime": the lips closed to finish. "Line" ends with the tongue tip on the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, /m/ finishes with the lips closed; /n/ finishes with the tongue tip on the ridge and the lips open. The preceding vowel also glides slightly differently.
quests.mouthPosition: For /m/ end with closed lips. For /n/ end with the lips open and the tongue tip touching the ridge.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the vowel end rounded or spread?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "moan": the vowel closed to a round. "Main" closes to a spread /ɪ/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /eɪ/ glides forward and up to /ɪ/ with spread lips; /əʊ/ glides back and up to /ʊ/ with rounded lips. They move in opposite directions.
quests.mouthPosition: For /eɪ/ finish with the lips slightly spread. For /əʊ/ finish with the lips pushed forward into a small round.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel is identical. What happens at the very end?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "bang" ended with the back of the tongue raised. "Ban" ends with the tongue tip on the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The tongue touches at the front for /n/ and at the back for /ŋ/, so the vowel before it colours differently.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue tip behind the lower teeth for /ŋ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same vowel. Broad hush or thin hiss to start?
quests.explanation: You heard "shy": a broad hush with slightly rounded lips. "Sigh" begins with a sharp, thin hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʃ/ is a broader, lower-pitched hush made with the tongue pulled slightly back and the lips a little rounded; /s/ is a sharper, higher hiss with the tongue tip near the teeth and the lips spread.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ʃ/ round the lips slightly and pull the tongue back so the air flows over a wider channel. For /s/ spread the lips and bring the tongue tip close to the ridge behind your teeth.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to how long the vowel stays before the ending.
quests.explanation: "Lit" has a shorter vowel and closes with a crisp stop. "Lid" lasts a bit longer and closes softly.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, the vowel or sonorant before /d/ lasts longer than before /t/. /t/ is short and sharp; /d/ is longer, softer and partly voiced.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind the teeth. For /t/ shorten the vowel and stop at once; for /d/ hold the vowel longer and close softly.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same stress, same vowel. Is the ending a hiss or a buzz?
quests.explanation: The word was "advice": a hiss at the end, and a shorter final vowel. "Advise" ends with a buzz.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Word-final /z/ often loses some voicing, but it never loses the longer vowel before it.
quests.mouthPosition: Cut the vowel short before /s/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Two syllables with the beat on the first. Listen to the vowel in that strong syllable.
quests.explanation: In this phrase, "latter" opened the jaw wide in the strong syllable. "Letter" stays half open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ is a short mid-front vowel with the jaw only half open; /æ/ is more open and a little longer, with the jaw dropped and the tongue lowered at the front.
quests.mouthPosition: For /e/ open the jaw about halfway and keep the lips relaxed. For /æ/ drop the jaw further and spread the mouth slightly, as if beginning to yawn sideways.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both start open. How do they end?
quests.explanation: It was "mouse": the vowel closed with rounded lips. "Mice" closes with the lips spread.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen to the end of the vowel: an 'ee' close for /aɪ/, an 'oo' close for /aʊ/.
quests.mouthPosition: Notice what your lips do at the very end: they stay flat for /aɪ/ and purse for /aʊ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the tongue stop the air completely at the start?
quests.explanation: "Then" begins with the tongue tip lightly against the teeth and a continuous buzz. "Den" begins with a firm stop at the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ð/ is a voiced fricative with the tongue at the teeth and continuous airflow; /d/ is a stop with a complete closure at the ridge behind the teeth. Listen for continuous buzzing versus an abrupt burst.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ð/ put the tongue tip lightly against the teeth and let voiced air flow. For /d/ press the tongue tip to the ridge behind the teeth, stop the air and release.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Rounded lips, or lip against teeth?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "wow": the lips rounded and glided. "Vow" starts with a buzzing lip-on-teeth /v/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The lower lip touches the teeth only for /v/.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue relaxed for both.
